solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Rod for a fish

definitions.meaning: a rod is an old unit of length, five and a half yards, also called a pole
a freshwater fish with spiny fins, common in rivers and lakes

explanation.surface: An angler asks what kind of rod suits a particular fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses share one word: the old land-measuring unit equal to a rod, and the spiny freshwater fish.

clue.text: Idly see about if they're open?

definitions.text: Idly see about if they're open?

indicators.note: about means scattered around, so the letters of the two words before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone half-awake glances around to check whether the eyes are open.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does double duty: the letters of 'Idly see' rearranged give the answer, and you can only idly see about when these are open.
explanation.definitionFit: The folds of skin over the eyes must be raised before anyone can look around, even idly.

clue.text: Stores for plant company with oddly chosen ramps

indicators.note: oddly chosen means taking the first, third and fifth letters of the word ramps

explanation.surface: A firm picks out ramps, perhaps wild garlic, to store for planting.
explanation.definitionFit: A corm is a swollen underground stem base in which a plant such as a crocus stores food over winter.

clue.text: In toy race circuits go for a spin taking lead from Button

indicators.note: circuits means goes round, so the race word surrounds the other pieces

parts.note: to race is to tear along at speed
to eddy is to swirl round in a circle, as water does

indicators.note: lead from means the opening letter of the word Button

explanation.surface: Racing cars lap a circuit in a toy race led by the driver Jenson Button.
explanation.walkthrough: 'race' and 'circuits' suggest motor racing (Jenson Button is a British Formula One driver), but here race is a verb meaning to rush.
explanation.definitionFit: A stuffed bear is a classic soft toy for children, named after US president Theodore Roosevelt.

clue.text: A walk in the park if feeling ill is out of the question

indicators.note: is out of means the following letters are removed from the word for feeling ill

parts.note: queasy means feeling sick or nauseous
QU is a standard abbreviation for question

explanation.surface: A walk in the park is out of the question if you are feeling unwell.
explanation.definitionFit: A walk in the park is an idiom for something requiring no effort, a simple task.

clue.text: Edge of tarn a long time after duck flies

indicators.note: after places the edge-and-era pieces behind the duck word

parts.note: to duck is to dip quickly under water

indicators.note: edge of means the first letter of the word tarn

parts.note: an era is a long period of time

explanation.surface: A duck dives at the edge of a mountain lake, long after the event.
explanation.definitionFit: Diptera is the zoological order of two-winged insects, including houseflies, gnats and mosquitoes.

clue.text: Butterfly's black on outer edges with general effect of colours

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
rims are the outer edges of something round
the tone of a picture is its overall effect of colour and shade

explanation.surface: A butterfly with black wing edges and a general colouring is described.
explanation.definitionFit: The brimstone is a yellow European butterfly, often the first to appear in spring.

clue.text: A neighbouring community with great differences and eternal rioting

definitions.text: A neighbouring community with great differences

indicators.note: rioting means running wild, so the letters of eternal are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Next-door neighbours with deep differences are locked in endless riots.
explanation.definitionFit: In ecology an alterne is a plant community sharply different from an adjacent one, occurring side by side.

clue.text: A barely-seen practice

parts.note: barely-seen looks like rarely seen, but means seen bare, unclothed

explanation.surface: Some custom is so uncommon it is hardly ever witnessed.
explanation.walkthrough: Barely-seen reads as scarcely observed; the pun is on people being seen bare.
explanation.definitionFit: Naturism is the habit of going about without clothes, so its followers are seen in the buff.

clue.text: Dupes fear mobile getting pinched by unworthy people

indicators.note: getting pinched by means held tight within the word for unworthy people

parts.note: duds are useless or worthless people

indicators.note: mobile means moving about, so the letters of fear are rearranged

explanation.surface: Worthless people fear that a mobile phone will be stolen by those who dupe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mobile' looks like a phone but is the signal to rearrange fear.
explanation.definitionFit: To dupe someone is to trick them; to defraud is to cheat someone out of money or property.

clue.text: Covers surface with colour, probably at least a litre covering area

indicators.note: covering means the pints word wraps round the letter for area

parts.note: two or more pints come to over a litre, since a pint is about 0.57 litres

explanation.surface: A decorator works out that covering a surface will take at least a litre of paint.
explanation.definitionFit: To paint is to apply colour to a surface, as a decorator does to a wall.

clue.text: Colourful plant rumoured to be brought back to China oddly

indicators.note: brought back means the word for rumoured is written backwards

parts.note: rumoured to be means said to be

indicators.note: oddly means taking the first, third and fifth letters of the word China

explanation.surface: A colourful plant is rumoured to have been brought back to China.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought back' seems to describe a plant collector's import, but it turns only the rumour word round.
explanation.definitionFit: Diascia, or twinspur, is a South African flowering plant with pink or coral blooms grown in gardens.

clue.text: Teaching graduate observed for report — consequence of lying over a long term?

definitions.text: consequence of lying over a long term?

parts.note: a BEd is a Bachelor of Education, a teaching degree

indicators.note: for report means the word that follows sounds like the spoken word for observed

parts.note: observed means saw

explanation.surface: A newly qualified teacher saw something worth reporting, and a long-term lie had consequences.
explanation.walkthrough: In standard southern British speech saw and sore are pronounced the same. 'lying over a long term' suggests deceit but means lying in bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A pressure ulcer forms on the skin of a patient confined to bed for a long period.

clue.text: Maybe a pig's trough seen in middle of barbecue

indicators.note: seen in means the trough word sits inside the middle pair of letters
middle of means the central two letters of the word barbecue

parts.note: a rut is a long narrow trough or groove

explanation.surface: A pig's feeding trough appears at the centre of a barbecue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trough' points to a pig's feeding trough, but means RUT; the middle of barbecue is BE.
explanation.definitionFit: A pig is an animal, and brute is a general word for a beast, so a pig is an example.

clue.text: Yielding and miserable after losing their heads — Retreat!

indicators.note: losing their heads means each of the two words drops its first letter

parts.note: easy can mean yielding, giving way readily
glum means miserable, downcast

explanation.surface: Soft and gloomy troops, having lost their nerve, are ordered to retreat.
explanation.walkthrough: EASY and GLUM each lose their first letter, E and G.
explanation.definitionFit: An asylum is a place of refuge or sanctuary, which is one sense of a retreat.

clue.text: Article is about international public relations and I can see what they're saying

definitions.text: I can see what they're saying

indicators.note: is about means the article word goes round the next pieces

parts.note: a leader is a newspaper's main editorial article

explanation.surface: A news article covers international public relations, and the writer claims to understand what is being said.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Article' looks like THE or AN, but here it is a newspaper LEADER.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who reads lips follows speech by watching mouth movements, so they see what is said.

clue.text: Sound of grass in the water captivating adult and child

indicators.note: captivating means holding inside, so the grass word encloses the next pieces

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass that grows in water
A is the abbreviation for adult, as in film ratings
a son is a child

explanation.surface: The rustle of reeds in water charms a grown-up and a youngster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like a noise, matching the surface; it is the adjective meaning logical.
explanation.definitionFit: A sound argument is well-founded and logical, just as a reasoned one is.

clue.text: Intention to have growing medium put around veg seedling perhaps?

indicators.note: put around means the growing medium word encloses the intention word

parts.note: peat is a growing medium used in compost
a plan is an intention

explanation.surface: A gardener means to put compost around a young vegetable plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A young plant that will produce peas is a vegetable seedling, hence the 'perhaps' for an example.

clue.text: On exhibition in the Tate, a Tintoretto to etch

indicators.note: on exhibition in means the letters are on show within the following words

explanation.surface: A Tintoretto painting on display in the Tate gallery is used to etch.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across tatE A TINTOretto.
explanation.definitionFit: To etch is to corrode a surface with acid, wearing it away gradually.

clue.text: Eternity after what's done for unfortunate hunter

indicators.note: after places the eternity word behind the deed word

parts.note: an act is something done, a deed
an aeon is an immensely long time, close to eternity

explanation.surface: An eternity passes after a deed for an unlucky huntsman.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Actaeon was a hunter who saw Artemis bathing and was turned into a stag and torn apart by his hounds.

clue.text: At last French expressions comprehended for heating units …

indicators.note: comprehended means contained, so the expressions word encloses the letter

parts.note: terms are words or expressions

indicators.note: at last means the final letter of the word French

explanation.surface: French expressions are finally understood when discussing heating units.
explanation.definitionFit: A therm is a British unit of heat equal to 100,000 British thermal units, used for gas bills.

clue.text: The small church over there displaying traditional roof?

parts.note: that points to something distant, over there, as opposed to this one here
CH is the short form of church

explanation.surface: A small church in the distance has a traditional roof.
explanation.definitionFit: A roof of straw or reeds is the traditional covering of an English country cottage.

clue.text: Turn over by unit in Dortmund plant

parts.note: to mull is to turn something over in the mind
ein is German for one, a unit, and Dortmund is a German city

explanation.surface: Someone turns over a unit in a German city's plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Mullein is a tall plant with woolly leaves and yellow flower spikes, of the genus Verbascum.

clue.text: … and French clipped accent around the boulevards?

indicators.note: around means the shortened accent word goes round the French word
clipped means cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: stress is accent, the emphasis on a syllable
et is French for and

explanation.surface: French spoken with a clipped accent is heard around the Paris boulevards.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis joins this to the previous clue, so 'and French' reads on from it while meaning the French word for and.
explanation.definitionFit: Boulevards are broad urban roads, a kind of street, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Moral tale of father and the Mob bumping off half the bishops

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father

indicators.note: bumping off means killing, so a letter is removed from the mob word

parts.note: the mob, a disorderly crowd, is the rabble
bishops abbreviate to BB, and half of that is one B

explanation.surface: Father and the Mafia bump off bishops, which makes a moral story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Mob' suggests the Mafia, but means RABBLE, which loses one of its two Bs.
explanation.definitionFit: A parable is a short story teaching a moral or religious lesson, like those told by Jesus.

clue.text: Maybe penpals at first spell incorrectly

parts.note: amis is French for friends, and pen pals are friends by letter

indicators.note: at first means the opening letter of the word spell

explanation.surface: Pen pals may spell words incorrectly at first.
explanation.definitionFit: Amiss means wrongly or astray, as in 'something went amiss'.

clue.text: This drive with special large opening one would have to spend a lot on

indicators.note: with an opening means the special-and-large letters stand at the front of this drive, so removing them from the spending word leaves it
with an opening means the special-and-large letters stand at the front of this drive, so removing them from the spending word leaves it

parts.words: one would have to spend a lot on
parts.note: to splurge is to spend extravagantly

explanation.surface: A special drive with a large opening is something you would have to spend heavily on.
explanation.walkthrough: An unusual construction: the clue says this answer, with the abbreviations for special and large at its start, becomes the word for extravagant spending.
explanation.definitionFit: A drive is a strong inner impulse, and so is an urge.

clue.text: Nervous it might be done badly by Georgia

indicators.note: badly means poorly made, so the letters of done are rearranged

parts.note: GE is the international code for the country Georgia

explanation.surface: Someone is anxious that a job might be botched by a Georgian.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling jumpy or tense is a common idiom for being nervous.

clue.text: Shrunk back and patched up with no charge taken

indicators.note: taken means removed, so the no-charge letters come out of the patched-up word

parts.note: two people who patch up a quarrel are reconciled

explanation.surface: Someone flinched after a quarrel was settled with no fee charged.
explanation.definitionFit: To recoil is to draw back in fear or disgust, to shrink away.

clue.text: Bolt and maybe Bolt's celebration of coming first

indicators.note: coming first means the celebration word goes in front

parts.note: a do is a party or celebration
Usain Bolt is a runner, the Jamaican sprinter, so Bolt is, for example, one of these

explanation.surface: Usain Bolt makes his famous celebration after winning a race.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'Bolt' is the verb, to flee; the second is the sprinter Usain Bolt. To leave without paying is British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: To bolt is to run off suddenly, and the slang phrase means to flee, often without paying.

clue.text: Taking drugs — or not if official who knows the score appeared first

indicators.note: appeared first means the official word would stand in front, so removing it from the refusing word leaves this answer

parts.note: refusing means not taking
a ref, short for referee, is the match official who keeps track of the score

explanation.surface: A sports official discovers whether a player is on drugs or not.
explanation.walkthrough: An unusual construction: 'or not' says that with the referee in front the answer turns into its opposite, declining.
explanation.definitionFit: Using is slang for taking illegal drugs regularly.
